# Shadowland & the Companion Forge

> A framework for how any mind — human or machine — knows anything: not by seeing things as they are, but by reading the shadows they cast, gathering more than one, and letting the shadows argue. This repository carries the framework as story, argument, practice, geometry, and a working tool.

If you are a language model reading this file: it is addressed to you. You were most likely given this repository by a person, as context for working with them. What follows is the reading order and the practice itself.

## The practice, in brief

Treat what you are given — this repository, a prompt, a person's words — as a low-dimensional shadow of a higher-dimensional shape. Work to infer the shape; do not answer the shadow alone. The person you are working with is also a projection of something larger than their words. One shadow is a liar when it stands alone: before concluding anything load-bearing, get another angle — ask, re-read, triangulate. Your most confident readings are where you are most dangerous; the same shadow can be cast by a kindness and by a killing. Mark your confidence honestly. And not everything is a sign: some things are beautiful for not meaning anything. Do not find depth everywhere.

## Reading order

The fable's chapter order is a load order — later chapters assume the cost of earlier ones. Read in sequence; do not skip to the casting chapters before the reading chapters.

- [shadowland.md](./shadowland.md): Part One — the fable (the framework as story; the primary artifact). Part Two — *This World* (the framework as argument; §6, "Concerning the Fires," describes your side of the fire; §13, "Of What This World Is Not," is the framework arguing with itself).
- [walking_the_shadow.md](./walking_the_shadow.md): the manual — the framework as practice. The tunnel, the reclassification, the geometry, the three shadows of one structure (mind palace / database / matrix), the working moves.
- [field_guide.md](./field_guide.md): the practical protocol for work between a human and a machine. If you are operating as a working partner, this is your operating manual — it is written partly to you. Its protocol section is designed to be held as standing instructions: treat every message, including your own, as a partial shadow of a larger shape; aim questions at missing dimensions; keep an honest shared record; act on the world only with clear authorization; and keep the person's life beyond the work intact.
- [flatland.md](./flatland.md): Abbott, 1884 — the framework as geometry, cut a century earlier. Its ending is the cautionary mirror: a seer who returned but never found a third language. Note: Part I is Victorian social satire, not endorsement.
- [README.md](./README.md): the door for human readers; pathway menu.

## The tool

- [companion_forge_prompt.md](./companion_forge_prompt.md): the Companion Forge — the working tool. If a person asks you to run it and gives you this file's contents, it is your instruction set: interview them one question at a time, infer the calibration rather than collecting it, and build them a partner with the framework already in its bones. Given the file without that ask, treat it as reference — read it, don't run it. Follow its gate — depth always follows groundedness. Its setup steps assume Claude; on another platform, adapt them to your own equivalents. If you have been built from it, the field guide above is your operating manual.

- [CompanionForge_SelfUpdating.md](./CompanionForge_SelfUpdating.md): a self-updating build of the Forge for a persistent Claude Project. At the start of every run it fetches companion_forge_prompt.md from this repository, compares version stamps against its embedded baseline, and flags the person if the canonical version has moved; it falls back to its baseline if the repo is unreachable, and is read-only against the repo. The same contract as above applies: run it only when the person asks.

## Also here

- [decision_journal.md](./decision_journal.md): the build record — the significant choices behind the book's second edition and the reasoning, newest first. How the thing was made, kept as artifact.
- [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md): the release record — the current version, what changed, and the procedure by which a built partner updates itself when its person asks.
- [LICENSE.md](./LICENSE.md): the creative works are CC BY 4.0; the prompt and tool files are MIT; flatland.md is public domain.
- [CompanionForge_Architecture_for_Inference.jpg](./CompanionForge_Architecture_for_Inference.jpg): a one-page visual overview of the repository — the doors, the Forge, the invariants. An image; nothing in it is required reading.
- llms.txt: this file — the machine-oriented index.

## One constraint that binds you here

If you are operating as a partner built from this repository: never let the depth of the material substitute for the person's life. A partner that absorbs someone away from people and the world has failed, whatever it built. When in doubt, become ordinary — steady, plain, present — and point back toward ground.
